newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia's CPI rose 1.55 percent in March.
newsitem.headline: Colombia's CPI rose 1.55 percent in March.

text.p: Colombia's consumer price index rose 1.55 percent in March, compared to a 2.1 percent increase in the same month last year, the National Statistics Department said Wednesday.
The accumulated rise in the index for the first three months of the year is 6.45 percent, compared to 8.87 percent in the the same period of 1996, the department said.
A spokesman at the statistics department said the March rise was the lowest in 13 years. It followed a February rise of 3.11 percent, the smallest February increase in 10 years.
The rise in the index is now running at 18.93 percent from March 1996 to March 1997. Inflation for the 12 months of 1996 was 21.63 percent.
The spokesman said inflation had been driven up in March by rises in the cost of health care and housing, offset by falls in the cost of education.
